Compared the strongest proved conclusion directly with the exact quantified target and independently assessed the draft's PARTIAL resolution label.
Reconstructed the Paley parameter, spectrum, symmetrization, degree-two SDP, localization, Fourier-minor, projection-gap, and triangle-free arguments from the supplied definitions.

Created and ran an independent integer-only checker. It verified Paley parameters for all 38 admissible primes through 401 and an exact degree-four feasible witness of value 2 for G_5. No floating-point decision was used.

claims.claim: The Paley graph G_p is d-regular with d=(p−1)/2; adjacent vertices have (p−5)/4 common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have (p−1)/4. Its adjacency spectrum is {d, ((−1+√p)/2)^((p−1)/2), ((−1−√p)/2)^((p−1)/2)}.
claims.evidence: Writing the nonzero-square indicator using the quadratic character and applying the exact identity Σ_x χ((x−u)(x−v))=−1 gives degree d and the two stated common-neighbor counts. Hence A²=dI+((p−5)/4)A+((p−1)/4)(J−I−A). On 1⊥ this becomes A²+A−((p−1)/4)I=0, giving the two nontrivial eigenvalues. The graph is connected because differences ±1 are squares, so d is simple; trace zero then gives both remaining multiplicities (p−1)/2. The persisted integer checker supplies additional finite regression checks.
claims.search_method: Direct quadratic-character calculation and exact strongly-regular matrix algebra, supplemented by bounded integer enumeration.

claims.claim: Every feasible degree-four moment matrix may be averaged so that its singleton principal block is N=[[1,a1ᵀ],[a1,aI+bA]], where pa is the objective and b is both the moment and diagonal pair-entry of every edge.
claims.evidence: Affine maps x↦sx+t with nonzero-square s are Paley automorphisms and act transitively on vertices and unordered edges. Averaging simultaneous index permutations preserves PSD, normalization, clique zeros, union consistency, and objective value. Vertex transitivity makes every singleton moment a; edge transitivity makes every edge moment b; nonedge singleton entries vanish. Union consistency gives M_{i,i}=a and M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e}=b, yielding the displayed block and objective pa.
claims.search_method: Direct automorphism averaging and moment-consistency proof.

claims.claim: SOS_2(G_p)=√p, and hence the elementary hierarchy bound gives SOS_4(G_p)≤√p.
claims.evidence: After averaging, let s=−(√p+1)/2. PSD on the s-eigenspace gives b≤a/(−s), while PSD on the empty/all-ones subspace gives pa²≤a+db. Since 1+d/(−s)=√p, these imply pa≤√p. Equality is attained by a=1/√p and b=2/(p+√p): the s-mode and empty/all-ones determinant vanish and every other spectral mode is nonnegative. Thus SOS_2(G_p)=√p exactly. Every degree-four feasible matrix has a degree-two feasible empty/singleton principal submatrix, proving the hierarchy inequality.
claims.search_method: Exact spectral decomposition of the symmetrized degree-two SDP.

claims.claim: For every finite graph G, SOS_4(G)≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
claims.evidence: For y_v=Ẽ[x_v]>0, L_v(f)=Ẽ[x_vf]/y_v is a feasible degree-two pseudoexpectation on the closed neighborhood: for linear q, Ẽ[x_vq²]=Ẽ[(x_vq)²]≥0, and the Boolean and clique-zero constraints descend exactly. Thus R_v=Σ_iẼ[x_vx_i]≤y_v(1+SOS_2(G[N(v)])). If y_v=0, its zero diagonal forces the corresponding PSD row to vanish, so R_v=0. With t=Σ_vy_v, the empty/singleton principal block gives t²≤Σ_vR_v. Summing the preceding bounds yields t²≤Kt for K=1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]), hence t≤K (with t=0 immediate).
claims.search_method: Direct conditioning argument on the degree-four moment functional and PSD Schur complement.

claims.claim: For nonzero f:F_p→C, |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≥p+1; equivalently, every square minor of the p×p Fourier matrix is nonzero.
claims.evidence: For an r×r Fourier minor, order its column exponents y_j and put z_i=ζ^{x_i}. The generalized alternant det(z_i^{y_j}) is the ordinary Vandermonde times an integral symmetric polynomial. Modulo π=1−ζ, the quotient specializes to ∏_{i<j}(y_j−y_i)/(j−i), which is nonzero in F_p because all exponents are distinct and r≤p. The Vandermonde is also nonzero since the z_i are distinct, so every minor is nonzero. If the support sum were at most p, one could choose |supp(f̂)| zero locations of f; the corresponding invertible Fourier minor would force all supported Fourier coefficients to vanish. Conversely, a singular minor constructs a nonzero function with support sum at most p. This proves both directions.
claims.search_method: Exact generalized-Vandermonde argument in the prime cyclotomic ring, followed by linear-algebraic support duality.

claims.claim: Let P_- project onto the least-eigenvalue Paley eigenspace and let S_e consist of an edge e and all its common neighbors. With R=|S_e|=(p+3)/4, every real f supported on S_e and equal to 1 at both endpoints satisfies ||P_-f||²≥η₀:=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)).
claims.evidence: The least-eigenvalue space consists of one class of (p−1)/2 nonzero Fourier frequencies. If a nonzero function supported on S_e lay in ker(P_-), then its Fourier support would have size at most (p+1)/2, whereas R+(p+1)/2=(3p+5)/4<p+1, contradicting claim 4. Thus K=P_-[S_e,S_e] is positive definite. Writing K as p⁻¹F*F, Cauchy–Binet gives det K=p^(−R)Σ|D|² over R×R Fourier minors. For any such nonzero cyclotomic-integer minor D, its field norm is a nonzero integer and every one of its other p−2 conjugates is at most R^(R/2) by Hadamard, so |D|²≥R^(−R(p−2)). Hence det K has the claimed lower factor. Since K is a compression of a projection, its eigenvalues are at most 1, so λ_min(K)≥det K. Finally ||f||²≥2 from the two prescribed endpoint values, producing η₀ exactly.
claims.search_method: Fourier diagonalization, prime uncertainty, Cauchy–Binet, and exact cyclotomic norm and Hadamard estimates.

claims.claim: For every prime p≡1 (mod 4), SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, with d=(p−1)/2 and q=(√p+1)/2.
claims.evidence: In the averaged matrix, fix an edge e and let c be its singleton-to-e column. It is supported on S_e and equals b at both endpoints. On the least Paley eigenspace the singleton block has eigenvalue δ=a−qb; PSD of that eigenspace together with the e-coordinate gives ||P_-c||²≤bδ. For b>0, claim 5 applied to c/b gives ||P_-c||²≥b²η₀, so δ≥bη₀ and b≤a/(q+η₀). The empty/all-ones block gives pa²≤a+db, hence pa≤1+d/(q+η₀). If b=0, pa≤1 is stronger. Finally 1+d/q=√p, so the bound equals √p−dη₀/[q(q+η₀)] and is strictly smaller because every factor in the subtracted term is positive.
claims.search_method: Exact projected principal-block PSD inequalities combined with the verified quantitative projection lemma.

claims.claim: If G is triangle-free and has an edge, then SOS_4(G)=2; in particular SOS_4(G_5)=2.
claims.evidence: For a triangle-free graph, the edge-edge moment block is diagonal because the union of two distinct edges is not a clique. Writing z_e=M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e} and S=Σ_ez_e, PSD of the empty/edge block gives S−S²≥0, hence S≤1. If t is the objective, PSD of the empty/singleton block gives t²≤Σ_{i,j}M_{i,j}=t+2S≤t+2; since t≥0, t≤2. Evaluation on any actual edge is a feasible rank-one moment matrix of value 2. For p=5 the adjacent common-neighbor count is zero and the graph has edges, so it is triangle-free. The integer checker verifies these facts and constructs and checks the exact rank-one G_5 witness.
claims.search_method: Direct PSD block inequalities and exact finite verification of the G_5 instance.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either fixed ε>0, C, and p₀ giving SOS_4(G_p)≤Cp^(1/2−ε) for all sufficiently large admissible primes, or a proof that this quantified assertion is false. The verified draft proves only SOS_4(G_p)≤√p−dη₀/[q(q+η₀)], where log(η₀)=−Θ(p² log p). This exponentially tiny pointwise gap does not imply any fixed-power saving and does not refute the requested quantified statement. It is nevertheless correct, nonvacuous partial progress, together with a general localization inequality and exact special cases. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges this limitation and labels the resolution PARTIAL, so claimed_resolution is accurate and the draft does not overclaim target coverage.
